To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the WGSs of the HV strains KPi261, KP4010 and KPB4011 were completed, and the genes associated with virulence were found.

the prevalence of hypermucoid Klebsiella strains in the Russian hospitals was 11%, and the WGS analysis of three hypermutant Klebsiella clinical strains revealed the presence of genes involved in virulence and antibiotic resistance.
the genomes of three HV strains of K. pneumoniaecarrying the capsular genes kpsMTII, rmpA, rmpA2and rmpA4were completed.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the first WGS of HV strains of K. pneumoniaecapsular types K1 and K20 isolated in Russia and the WGS of the HV K. pneumoniae K2 strain.
the first WGSs of HV K. pneumoniae strains from Russian hospitals, and the first WGS of a K. pneumoniae freshwater strain.
the first report of the WGSs and comparative analysis of the K1, 2, 20 and 57 capsular serotypes of HV K. pneumoniae strains isolated from clinical and nonclinical environments.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the K. pneumoniaes of different serotypes, including K1, K57, K20 and the K2 capsular type, are characterized by similar virulence-associated gene clusters and the ability to produce biofilms.
KPi261 and KPB40110 strains are closely related and are more similar to each other than to the K. pneumonia strains of other serotypes.
the WGSs of the K. pneumoniae strains KPi261, KP4010 and KPB9 isolated from clinical and environmental sources in Russia are available in the GenBank database.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the WGS data for the K. pneumoniaes KPi261, KBP4010 and KPB4011 strains would be useful for the development of new molecular typing methods for HV K. pneumoniae strains and the identification of virulence genes.
HV strains are not uncommon among K. pneumoniae clinical isolates in Russia.
the K. pneumonia strains isolated in the Russian hospitals are genetically diverse, and the K2 and K1 serotypes are the most common.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the WGSs of the K. pneumonea HV strains from Russia were similar to those of the K. pneunomiae HV strains from other countries.
WGSs of HV strains can provide valuable data on the prevalence and characteristics of these strains in the environment, as well as on the virulence factors of these strains.
the HV strains are not only associated with a high risk of infection, but are also highly virulent and resistant to a wide range of antibiotics, and thus pose a serious threat for the public health.
